sources.headline: India bars sugarcane-based ethanol from 2026-27 procurement tender to safeguard sugar supplies
sources.content: New Delhi: State-run oil marketing companies have excluded ethanol produced from sugarcane juice, sugar syrup and B-heavy molasses from their latest procurement tender for the 2026-27 supply year, following government directions to halt sugar diversion for fuel amid concerns over domestic availability and prices.Bharat Petroleum Corporation Ltd (BPCL), acting on behalf of the oil marketing companies, issued the tender on October 16 seeking bids for approximately 11 billion litres of ethanol. The volume is intended to support the nationwide target of blending 20 per cent ethanol in petrol during the supply year that runs from November 2026 to October 2027.The tender document states: “The Government of India has issued directions that sugar diversion for ethanol be reduced to zero for ethanol supply year 2026-27.” It adds that “no offers have been sought for ethanol produced from sugarcane juice, sugar or sugar syrup and B-heavy molasses.”Instead, the companies will accept bids for ethanol made from maize, broken rice, surplus rice procured by the Food Corporation of India, and C-heavy molasses. The procurement price for maize-based ethanol has also been reduced to Rs 68.86 per litre from Rs 71.86, cutting the incentive from Rs 5.79 to Rs 2.79 per litre.Sugar, ethanol and the policy balance: Why India needs predictable rules over crisis controlsThe restrictions come after poor rainfall in major sugar-producing states such as Maharashtra and Karnataka raised the prospect of lower output. India, the world’s largest sugar consumer, has faced rising domestic prices and concerns that continued diversion of cane and sugar into ethanol could tighten food supplies.The ethanol-blended petrol programme has relied on both sugarcane- and grain-based feedstock to cut crude oil imports and reduce vehicle emissions. India has rolled out E20 fuel — petrol containing up to 20 per cent ethanol — as the national standard. Officials view the latest tender as an effort to maintain the blending targets while prioritising sugar availability for consumption and containing prices.

primary_source.headline: '56-inch ka seena kahan hai': Rahul Gandhi slams Modi-Shah, CEC over 'vote chori'
primary_source.content: Congress leader Rahul Gandhi on Sunday accused Prime Minister Narendra Modi of orchestrating alleged “vote theft” behind the scenes, claiming that Union Home Minister Amit Shah operationalised it and Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar implemented it.Addressing a rally in Margao in South Goa on the concluding day of the Congress's 'Goy Rakhon Yatra', Gandhi alleged that Modi, Shah and Kumar were facing mounting pressure over the party's allegations of electoral malpractice.“There is no confusion anymore. Gyanesh Kumar implements the vote theft, Amit Shah operationalises it, and Prime Minister Narendra Modi does the entire planning from behind the scenes,” Gandhi said.The Leader of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha warned that the three would face justice over the alleged irregularities. He also claimed that the Congress had evidence of electoral malpractice in several states, including Madhya Pradesh, Haryana, Karnataka, Chhattisgarh, Maharashtra, West Bengal and Assam.“PM Modi, Amit Shah and CEC Gyanesh Kumar will face justice and pay the price for what they have done,” he said.Gandhi had led protests against the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) exercise and Kumar in New Delhi. He alleged that opposition votes had been deleted, votes added in favour of the ruling party, and voters shifted between districts or brought in from other states.Claiming that more than 45 defamation cases had been filed against him, including by people associated with Modi and Shah, Gandhi said no case had been filed over his allegations of vote theft. He suggested that the government was reluctant to pursue the matter legally because it could lead to a full-fledged legal battle.Urging voters to give the Congress a full majority in the 2027 Goa Assembly elections, Gandhi called on party workers to continue engaging with people across the state.Rahul Gandhi to address Goa rally as Congress wraps up 28-day 'Goy Rakhon Yatra'“You think about Goa. In Delhi, in a short while, we will deal with Narendra Modi and Amit Shah. You don't need to worry about that. The work is underway; their expiry date is approaching,” he said.Gandhi also accused the BJP-led Union government of favouring industrialists Gautam Adani and Mukesh Ambani by awarding them infrastructure projects, land and other economic opportunities in exchange for political support and publicity.“This is their system. This is how their system works: give billionaires money, give them contracts, give them land. In return, the billionaires do their marketing,” he alleged.Turning to Goa, Gandhi accused the state government of taking land from farmers and economically weaker sections and transferring it to outsiders and associates. He alleged that the cancellation of the regional master plan had enabled the government to facilitate such transfers, putting the state's natural resources and cultural heritage at risk.“Goa is a paradise, one of the most beautiful places in the country, with a great culture,” he said, alleging that its land was being handed over to billionaires.The Congress leader further claimed that Goa had the country's highest unemployment rate, forcing young people to seek opportunities abroad. He accused the BJP government of dismantling the state's employment structure and described its functioning as a “special Goa model of corruption”, drawing a comparison with the Gujarat model associated with Modi.On education, Gandhi criticised the alleged use of force against student protesters in Delhi and accused the BJP and the Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS) of influencing university appointments. He said students were raising concerns over electoral malpractice, unemployment, education costs and inflation.“This country does not belong to any one organisation. This country does not belong to the RSS. This country does not belong to the BJP. This country belongs to the people of India,” he said.Gandhi added that Goa belonged to its people, not its chief minister or ministers, and called for access to education, healthcare and employment, alongside environmental protection.Taking a swipe at the Prime Minister, Gandhi questioned the absence of Modi's often-cited “56-inch seena”, saying he could not stand in front of his political opponents.He urged Congress workers to continue the party's fight against the BJP's ideology beyond the conclusion of the yatra.The 27-day 'Goy Rakhon Yatra', led by Goa Congress leaders Yuri Alemao and Girish Chodankar, began on September 22 and covered all 40 Assembly constituencies in the coastal state. The party said the campaign aimed to protect Goa's land, environment, cultural heritage and identity while strengthening its grassroots presence ahead of the 2027 Assembly elections.(With PTI Inputs)

primary_source.headline: Explained | Govt caps trade margins on 137 cancer drugs at 30%: NPPA
primary_source.content: The Ministry of Chemicals and Fertilisers has announced a price cap of 30 per cent on the trade margins of 137 cancer medicines, over the cost of the drug at the first point, either to a stockist/distributor or the hospital. These margins will apply when the drugs are sold directly to them by a manufacturer.&nbsp;The National Pharmaceutical Pricing Authority (NPPA), in an order dated October 17, has directed manufacturers to submit the revised MRP within seven days. "The revised prices shall come into effect from November 9," the gazette notification stated.&nbsp;Impact on cancer drug pricesAn analysis of pharmaceutical market data indicates that non-scheduled anti-cancer drugs carry an average trade mark-up of approximately 170 per cent, with mark-ups of up to 700 per cent in certain cases, according to an NPPA meeting conducted earlier. This order is expected to reduce the MRP of non-scheduled anti-cancer drugs by 70 per cent, depending on their current price structures.&nbsp;The 137 identified non-scheduled anti-cancer drugs include immunotherapy drugs used for treating over 20 types of cancers, denosumab used by breast and prostate cancer patients, pegfilgrastim, which is used to prevent neutropenia in cancer patients and bevacizumab, which is the approved drug to treat colon, ovarian, and cervical cancer. With this notification, MRP of widely used anti-cancer drugs such as pembrolizumab, durvalumab and osimertinib is expected to become more accessible for cancer patients.Anti-cancer drug prices to come down as govt caps trade margins at 30%Centre caps trade margins on cancer medicines at 30% of MRPMarket overview: scheduled vs non-scheduled drugsCurrently, the anti-cancer drugs market comprises nearly 225 drugs and 500 formulations, with an annual turnover of around Rs 12,500 crore. Of this, scheduled cancer drugs that come under price control account for approximately Rs 2,250 crore, with the balance comprising non-scheduled drugs.To ensure that these life-saving medicines remain available, manufacturers of non-scheduled anti-cancer drugs will be required to maintain their current production levels. NPPA has clearly stated: "The manufacturers of the formulations are required to maintain the present production levels. Any manufacturer intending to lower the average monthly production levels will seek prior permission from NPPA. Further, any manufacturer intending to discontinue production of the above-said formulations shall furnish information to NPPA."&nbsp;How is the new price calculated?The manufacturers of non–scheduled formulations, selling branded or generic or both the versions of formulations at MRP higher than the MRP should revise their prices using this formula:&nbsp; MRP of the product = Price to Stockist or Price to Distributor x {1 + (Trade Margin/(100 − Trade Margin))} + Applicable GST.&nbsp;Citing an example, NPPA explained: For a non-scheduled anti-cancer formulation with current MRP: Rs 300 + Applicable GST. However, the price to a distributor is Rs 70. Maximum allowable revised MRP as per formula shall be: Rs70x{1+(30/(100−30))} = Rs 100 + Applicable GST.&nbsp;The notification has also clarified: "All the existing manufacturers of formulations having MRP lower than the MRP so computed … shall maintain their existing MRP."

primary_source.content: As civil war has left their country in ruins, many young Sudanese have turned to artisanal mining. stories.primary_headline: Oil facilities hit in deadly overnight attack on St Petersburg

primary_source.headline: Oil facilities hit in deadly overnight attack on St Petersburg
primary_source.content: The St Petersburg Oil Terminal was among targets hit in the city overnight The region's Governor Alexander Beglov said fires were being extinguished at the St Petersburg Oil Terminal and the Ruchyi oil depot following the attack, which also injured at least five. A logistics centre belonging to Ozon - known as Russia's Amazon - and a data centre belonging to Facebook equivalent VKontakte were also hit. Kyiv has not yet commented on the strikes. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky said on Saturday morning that Russia had targeted his country's energy sector 76 times since Donald Trump declared an "energy ceasefire" last week. Ukraine had paused its strikes on Russian oil facilities - which it says are to limit the main revenue stream for Moscow's war effort - for three days after the announcement, while accusing Russia of continuing. It then resumed strikes earlier this week, drawing the ire of Trump, who called for a truce to facilitate a deal he struck with his Russian counterpart Vladimir Putin to supply diesel.

stories.primary_headline: ‘4,000 people minding our own business’: four decades on, Falklands again face a hostile Argentina

primary_source.headline: ‘4,000 people minding our own business’: four decades on, Falklands again face a hostile Argentina
primary_source.content: Facing a slump in the polls, Argentina’s president is making economic attacks on the islands’ oil industry, and suggesting its key fisheries industry could be next A dozen local people and a uniformed military police officer (“Do you mind if I sit in?”) took their seats at the back of the handsome wood-panelled courtroom that doubles as the Falkland Islands’ legislative assembly. Outside, it was a typically blowy early evening. It may nominally be spring in the south Atlantic, but Stanley harbour, with its dark grey water speckled with historical shipwrecks, was a cauldron of swells and churn.Six of the assembly’s eight members – five men, one woman – waited patiently at a row of desks and microphones. The heating had been turned up to just short of uncomfortable. Behind them, a portrait of King Charles. From the other walls, dusty photographs of governors, of varying popularity, gazed disinterestedly at the scene. Continue reading...

As pounding waves driven by late-summer storms in the Pacific devour chunks of the California coastline, some of San Clemente’s beaches are growing narrower, the sand increasingly eaten away. stories.primary_headline: Keralam Devaswom Minister dissatisfied with TDB preparations for Sabarimala pilgrimage

primary_source.headline: Keralam Devaswom Minister dissatisfied with TDB preparations for Sabarimala pilgrimage
primary_source.content: Thiruvananthapuram: Keralam Devaswom Minister K Muraleedharan on Sunday expressed dissatisfaction with the Devaswom Board's preparations for the upcoming annual Sabarimala pilgrimage season.The minister's remarks came a day after he and Chief Minister V D Satheesan visited the various places associated with the Sabarimala pilgrimage to review preparations and facilities for the upcoming season.After the review meeting, the CM said that all arrangements related to temple rituals and prasadam were under the control of the Devaswom Board, and its president has assured that there will be no shortage of prasadam or other facilities at the shrine.On Sunday, Muraleedharan told a TV channel that repair and renovation of the plant manufacturing the 'aravana payasam' prasadam has not been completed yet.He also said that there was an apparent lack of coordination between the Board and the police with regard to crowd control.BJP steps up attack on Keralam govt over Sabarimala arrangementsThe minister said that his two main concerns were regulating the large number of devotees who arrived for the pilgrimage and ensuring a sufficient supply of 'appam' and 'aravana' for the pilgrims.'Aravana' -- a thick, sweet dessert made from red rice, jaggery, ghee, cardamom powder, and ginger powder -- and 'appam' -- a traditional sweet rice cake/fritter made with ingredients like rice and jaggery -- are the two primary 'prasadam' at the Lord Ayyappa shrine at Sabarimala."I am not completely satisfied with the steps being taken to ensure the prasadam sufficiency. The contract for the rice has not yet been finalised by the Board. I have been told that the repair and renovation of the plant will be completed by November 5 and production will be started," Muraleedharan said.He said that he has told the Board to give specific attention to these issues.The minister said that 29,000 devotees reached the shrine on Saturday ahead of the commencement of the 'Thula masam' puja on Sunday and currently there were two lakh aravana in stock."I have told the Board to take extra care regarding the matter up to October 22 (when the shrine will close again). After that, they have to ensure things are much better," he said.The Sabarimala shrine will be open for five days during the 'Thula masam' -- the third month in the traditional Malayalam calendar -- from October 18 to October 22.Muraleedharan also said that there was a delay in the completion of temple maintenance works."The government is doing all that has to be done," he added.The Sabarimala Sree Dharma Sastha Temple will open on November 17 for the 41-day Mandalam pilgrimage season.
